shortDescription: Israel's Swish Ventures said on Thursday it has raised $250 million for its third venture capital fund, which it has now closed to new investors.

children: Israel's Swish Ventures said on Thursday it has raised $250 million for its third venture capital fund, which it has now closed to new investors.
Swish was founded in 2025 by Omri Casspi, the first Israeli to play in the National Basketball Association. He played between 2009 and 2019.
Swish's assets under management have grown to $800 million.
It has so far invested in 20 companies with a combined value of more than $60 billion. Eight of the companies are valued above $1 billion.
The new fund aims to invest in 12 companies with an average of $20 million per company, either as co-lead investor alongside another fund or as a participating investor.
It will focus on startups operating across cybersecurity, technology infrastructure, physical AI, defence, AI for industrial applications, and government technology.
Investments are made in the Seed and Series A stages, enabling it to continue investing through growth stages.
The fund's investors include existing Swish backers as well as new investors, including Sequoia Capital, U.S. institutional investors such as pension funds and American universities.
